tasks.short: Help staff on the floor with difficult or complicated duties, answer their procedure questions, and note recurring problems for training.

steps.what: Recreation supervisor provides staff with assistance in performing difficult or complicated duties
Staff look up routine procedures in the staff app on their phones
Recreation supervisor answers staff questions on procedures by phone and chat
Recreation supervisor notes recurring problems for training: on paper today, in a short form for the training plan after the change

tasks.design: Procedures for rides, equipment, first aid and closing sit in the staff app ({DOCS}) with short steps and photos, so staff look up routine answers and call the supervisor for the hard cases. The supervisor notes recurring problems in a short form for the training plan instead of on paper, which takes as long. Helping staff on the floor stays with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures sat in a binder in the office and staff called for every question.
tasks.enabler_now: Staff apps hold procedures on the phone.
tasks.still_hard: New seasonal staff do not know what to look for.
tasks.human_edge: Stepping in calmly when a guest situation escalates.

evidence.claim: Staff apps can hold procedures with photos on employees' phones.

assumptions: Boundary: from the staff request to training notes; training sessions are outside.
Input contract: procedures kept by the operations manager; fallback is the binder.
Floor help and noting recurring problems keep their full time; the notes are the supervisor's own first record. s2 keeps 60 because staff look up routine answers (s2l) and call only for hard cases.
Staff look up procedures in about the time a call took.
research_questions: Do routine calls to the supervisor fall?

incremental.description: Recreation supervisor keeps procedures in the app current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an experienced team with few routine questions, so calls drop little and s2 keeps 85 (2.3); high: many new seasonal staff look up routine answers (7.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check stock and condition of safety and activity equipment, make the requisition list, check it, send it to purchasing, and put away supplies on arrival.

steps.what: Recreation supervisor checks stock of supplies such as first aid kits and flash lights: counts on paper today; scans each shelf label and enters the count after the change
Recreation supervisor checks the condition of safety harnesses and equipment
Recreation supervisor makes the requisition list for supplies and equipment
Recreation supervisor checks the requisition
Recreation supervisor e-mails the requisition to purchasing
Recreation supervisor receives and puts away supplies

tasks.design: A stock list with reorder points in the purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}) is updated by scanning shelf labels and entering counts, and it proposes the requisition from the catalogue of contracted suppliers. Once the supervisor has checked it, the requisition goes to purchasing. Checking the condition of harnesses and other safety equipment stays with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock was counted on paper and requisitions typed in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Purchasing systems hold reorder points and supplier catalogues.
tasks.still_hard: Safety equipment must be replaced on condition, not only on count.
tasks.human_edge: Rejecting a harness that looks fine but has a worn stitch.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor checks proposals instead of building lists.

evidence.claim: Purchasing systems propose requisitions from reorder points and supplier catalogues.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stock room to supplies stored; supplier contracts are outside.
Input contract: catalogues loaded by purchasing; fallback is spreadsheets and e-mail.

Checking equipment condition and checking the requisition keep their full time. s1 keeps 80 because the scan finds the item row and counting stays. s3 keeps 40 because the system proposes quantities from reorder points and the supervisor adds what the condition check found.
Purchasing works from requisitions as it did from e-mails.
research_questions: Do stock-outs of first aid supplies fall?

incremental.description: Recreation supervisor adjusts reorder points each season as activities change.

approvals.approved_version: The requisition with items, quantities and contracted suppliers exactly as checked by the supervisor in s4, sent once to purchasing in the purchasing system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many items are outside the contracted catalogue, so the supervisor still writes much of the list and s3 keeps 70 (17.0); high: the catalogue covers most supplies (24.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend meetings with managers, read updates and memos, write a short update for workers, post it in the staff app, and explain changes at the shift briefing.

steps.what: Recreation supervisor meets with managers to stay informed of changes affecting workers
Recreation supervisor reads updates and memos by e-mail
Recreation supervisor writes a short update for workers
Recreation supervisor checks the final update before posting: changes as the managers stated them, dates and the shift it is for
Recreation supervisor posts the update: pins it on the staff notice board today; posts the checked update in the staff app for the shift after the change
Recreation supervisor explains changes at the shift briefing

tasks.design: Management updates go to one channel in the staff app ({CHAT}) instead of scattered e-mails, so the supervisor reads them in one place. The supervisor writes a short update for workers as today, checks it and posts it in the staff app for the shift. Meetings with managers and explaining changes at the briefing stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Updates came in many e-mails and were pinned on a paper notice board.
tasks.enabler_now: Staff apps carry updates to all workers' phones.
tasks.still_hard: Not every worker reads the app.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a change so the team accepts it.

reach.learn: Whether changes are known before the shift.

evidence.claim: Staff apps can carry updates to all workers' phones.
Tools that can watch attendance or performance need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the meeting agenda to workers informed; decisions by managers are outside.
Input contract: managers post in the staff app; fallback is e-mail and notice board.

Meetings, briefings, writing the update and the check before posting keep their full time. s2 keeps 70 because updates sit in one channel instead of scattered e-mails. s4 keeps 10 for posting in the app instead of walking to the notice board.
Workers read the app as they read the notice board.
research_questions: Are workers aware of changes before the shift more often?

incremental.description: Recreation supervisor checks who has not read urgent updates.

approvals.approved_version: The update text exactly as checked by the supervisor in s4c, posted once in the staff app for the named shift; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: managers keep sending e-mails, so updates stay scattered and s2 keeps 90 (5.6); high: managers post in the staff app (10.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with activity leaders about needs and problems, relay questions and decisions between managers and leaders, keep track of open questions, and represent leaders in meetings with managers.

steps.what: Recreation supervisor talks with leaders of recreational activities about their needs and problems
Activity leaders enter their questions in the shared request list in the staff app
Recreation supervisor serves as a point of contact relaying questions and decisions between managerial staff and leaders
Recreation supervisor keeps track of open questions on a paper list
Recreation supervisor represents activity leaders in meetings with managers

tasks.design: Questions from activity leaders go into a shared request list in the staff app ({WORKFLOW}) with an owner and status, so the supervisor relays fewer messages by hand and sees what is open. Talking with leaders and representing them stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions went by phone and e-mail and were tracked on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Request lists with owners and status are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Some questions need a conversation, not a ticket.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which leader's complaint signals a real safety issue.

evidence.claim: Request lists with owners and status can track questions between staff and managers.

assumptions: Boundary: from activity issues to leaders represented; manager decisions are outside.
Input contract: leaders and managers use the request list; fallback is phone and e-mail.
Conversations and meetings do not change.

Leaders enter a request (s2e) in about the time a message took. s2 keeps 60 because questions and answers sit on the list with an owner, so fewer messages are relayed by hand. s3 keeps 30 because the list replaces copying questions onto paper.
research_questions: Do open questions get closed sooner?

incremental.description: Recreation supervisor tidies the request list each week.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: managers keep answering by phone and e-mail, so the supervisor still relays and tracks much by hand; s2 keeps 80 and s3 keeps 60 (11.4); high: leaders and managers use the list (21.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The recreation supervisor keeps helping staff, checking equipment and linking managers and leaders; binders, paper lists and scattered e-mails shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor with more time on the floor.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Entertainment and Recreation Workers, Except Gambling Services
